description:
Programme or Project Overview

UMCG is seeking a postdoctoral researcher in neurobiology with a focus on multiple sclerosis. The researcher joins a laboratory studying the immunological and neurodegenerative mechanisms that drive disease progression in MS, using cellular models and human tissue material available through the centre's clinical programmes.

The postdoc will design and execute experiments linking immune-cell behaviour with neuroaxonal damage, analyse molecular datasets, and contribute to the group's translational agenda of identifying treatment-relevant mechanisms. The position is a salaried postdoctoral appointment under the CAO-UMC collective agreement, with mentoring towards independent research and grant writing.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a PhD in neurobiology, immunology, molecular biology or a related field, with demonstrated experience in cell-culture models, immunological assays and molecular data analysis. The group values candidates who bring both experimental rigour and the ability to work across clinical and basic-science boundaries. English is the working language of the laboratory, and the postdoc participates in the centre's neuroscience research school and international collaborations.

Highlights

  • Immunological mechanisms of multiple sclerosis
  • Neurodegeneration and neuroaxonal damage models
  • Cellular assays and human tissue research
  • Molecular and multi-omics data analysis
  • Translational research bridging clinic and laboratory
  • Salaried postdoc under the CAO-UMC collective agreement

About University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG)

UMCG is one of the largest university medical centres in the Netherlands and the academic hospital of the University of Groningen. It combines patient care with biomedical research and graduate education, organised around research institutes covering neuroscience, oncology, ageing, regenerative medicine and population health. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the Dutch collective agreement for university medical centres (CAO-UMC). Research and clinical vacancies, including physician-researcher tracks and technical R&D roles, are published on its recruitment portal werkenbijumcg.nl.
